bullets.title: Markets reverse: SPX -0.9%, 30yr yield 5.25%, dollar breaks 200-DMA
bullets.body: Thursday's session closed with S&P 500 down 0.9% (7,643) and Nasdaq down 1.04% as bond-buyback optimism faded. The 30-year Treasury yield rose 6bp to 5.25%; markets concluded Treasury's expanded buyback program addresses symptoms, not the $2T deficit. DXY broke below its 200-day MA for the first time in 3+ months. Pre-market Friday: S&P futures +0.40% to 7,693, with USD continuing to weaken and broader risk-on tone returning aided by Bitcoin's surge.

bullets.title: Treasury buybacks seen as insufficient; bond vigilantes unmoved, yields above pre-announcement levels
bullets.body: Bessent signaled potential expansion of long-dated debt buybacks beyond the announced $4B limit and pointed to a forthcoming fiscal-consolidation plan, but 30-year yields rose above pre-announcement levels—markets remain skeptical. Foreign official Treasury holdings at the Fed fell to $2.6T (14-year low); gold overtook Treasuries as the top central bank reserve asset (26.3% vs. 20.2%) for the first time since 1996. Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29) and Chairman Warsh's Aug 28 speech are the next key macro events.

bullets.title: Oil +5%+ weekly on Iran isolation campaign; Brent above $93, SPR at 43-year low
bullets.body: WTI settled at $87.83 (+2.3%) and Brent at $93.78 (+2.4%) as the Trump administration prepared what Bessent called the 'greatest coordinated economic isolation' of Iran, including secondary sanctions on foreign buyers. Iran's central bank governor separately said oil exports have stopped. Strait of Hormuz crossings remain at single-digit levels. The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell 5.3M barrels to 293.4M—a 43-year low.

bullets.title: Bitcoin best weekly gain in 3+ years; crypto ETF inflows surge, gold tracks third weekly gain
bullets.body: Bitcoin surged above $76,000 pre-market Friday (futures +5.6%), posting its best weekly run in 3+ years. The Treasury buyback announcement triggered a simultaneous 12% BTC rally, 4% gold gain, and 1% dollar decline—widely read as debasement trades. Spot gold rose to ~$4,562/oz, on track for a third consecutive weekly gain. Bitcoin and Ether ETF inflows were the largest since May and January respectively.

bullets.title: Fed policy risk asymmetric: 22V and Hedgeye warn market pricing too-easy Fed given 6.5% nominal GDP
bullets.body: 22V Research flagged increasing risk of tighter Fed policy and yield-curve flattening, arguing the market is pricing too-easy policy given 6.5% nominal GDP and 4.1% unemployment. The note recommends KRE put-spread hedges (Sept 73/68) as regionals have failed to make new highs. Hedgeye's SPX range is 7,610-7,835 with VIX expected to print new cycle lows near 13.90; Morgan Stanley sees unemployment rising to 4.3% by December as labor force participation normalizes.

bullets.title: Eurozone August PMI beats at 52.1; Germany slips to 51.0, France contracts at 48.8, periphery at 55.8
bullets.body: The Eurozone flash composite PMI rose to 52.1 in August (vs. 51.7 forecast), implying ~1.4% annualized growth per JPMorgan vs. their 1.25% Q3 GDP forecast. The data mask a widening core-periphery split: Germany fell to 51.0 and France contracted at 48.8, while ex-Germany/France rose to 55.8 on tourism. ECB's Kazaks signaled wage growth is gradually slowing and inflation expectations remain anchored, maintaining a data-dependent September stance. Goldman and JPMorgan strategists remain positive on European equities citing strong earnings.

bullets.title: Japan CPI at 2.0%, BOJ hike odds now ~80% for September; JGB yields surge across curve
bullets.body: Japan's July core CPI rose 1.8% YoY (overall 2.0%), accelerating for a second consecutive month. Markets now price ~80% probability of a BOJ hike in September. JGB yields rose sharply: 30-year +5.5bp to 4.06%, 20-year +6bp to 3.77%, 10-year +4bp to 2.885%. Japan's Finance Ministry is considering a 3.8% assumed interest rate for FY2027/28 debt servicing. Japan's July chip-making equipment billings rose 35.4% YoY and Taiwan export orders hit a record $97.94B (+61.9% YoY) driven by +88.9% US orders.

bullets.title: Bipartisan data-center opposition: Texas halts 1,800 projects; 75% of Americans oppose local builds
bullets.body: Texas Governor Abbott issued a directive halting up to 1,800 data center projects, while Pennsylvania is restricting development despite also offering permitting incentives for self-powered facilities. JPMorgan notes 75% of Americans oppose local data center development; the anti-datacenter movement is described as bipartisan and fast-moving. Goldman raised its US data center construction spend forecast 10% to $67B (2026) and $87B (2027) but regulatory supply constraints could ironically strengthen incumbent pricing power for operators like EQIX.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle validated: hyperscaler cloud hit $106B in Q2 (+43% YoY); token volumes double every 11 weeks
bullets.body: Combined AWS, Microsoft Intelligent Cloud, and Google Cloud Q2 revenue reached ~$106.3B, +43% YoY and +15% QoQ. OpenRouter token volumes exceed 4.5 quadrillion at a run rate doubling every ~11 weeks. JPMorgan notes the AI capex cycle is becoming 'more economically viable than six months ago,' with APAC AI spend projected to accelerate 29% to ~$250B over the next 12 months. Goldman raised data center construction forecasts 10% to $67B/$87B for 2026/27.

bullets.title: Broadcom seeking $60B+ in AI debt financing; AI ecosystem 'phantom leverage' now in trillions
bullets.body: Broadcom is in talks with Blackstone and Apollo to raise more than $60B ($60-70B senior secured + $30B junior tranche via SPV) to finance AI chip capacity for Anthropic and others, a deal that could reach $100B. JPMorgan flags growing 'phantom leverage' in the AI ecosystem—leases, purchase commitments, revenue-volume guarantees, and backstops stretching into trillions—treated differently by rating agencies and posing systemic risk if AI demand or utilization disappoints. Anthropic separately is preparing an IPO filing as soon as end of August, targeting a size matching or exceeding SpaceX's record.

bullets.title: Hedge funds rotating beyond AI into Financials, Energy; HF positioning at decade-highs in both sectors
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Prime data shows hedge funds rotating beyond AI into Health Care, Financials, and Energy, with positioning in the latter two at or near decade highs. Asia hedge funds are net selling Info Tech (17.5% overweight to MXAP, down from ~22% peak); Korea is the most net-sold market YTD. In Asia, China net allocation has recovered marginally to 6.9% while Japan allocations continue declining. Globally, fundamental L/S funds are up 14.1% YTD; systematics up 15.2%.

bullets.title: Software earnings season muted: 82.1% beat rate below historical average; true beat-and-raise at 44%
bullets.body: KeyBanc's enterprise software earnings tracker shows an 82.1% beat rate (vs. 83.7% historical average), with true beat-and-raise companies at only 44%—370bp below the four-quarter average. Median full-year raises are just $6M vs. $15M at the halfway point last year. Despite muted fundamentals, software stocks reacted positively (median T+1 +3.6%, T+7 +4.5%), suggesting multiple recovery on easier expectations. Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.8x FY+2 EV/Sales, down 1.5% YTD vs. S&P 500 +14.5%.

bullets.title: Consumer under pressure: WMT US comps decelerate to 2.6%; lower-income consumer weakening
bullets.body: Walmart US comps slowed to +2.6% in 2Q27 (vs. +4.1% in 1Q27) as lower-income consumers faced elevated gas prices and health/wellness deflation was a 125bp headwind. Tariff refunds of ~$0.06 EPS benefit will fully reverse in 3Q. WMT guided near-term comps to 2-3%. Ross Stores sharply contrasted: +10% comps driven by new and lapsed customers with FY26 comp guidance raised to +8.5-9.5%. The K-shaped consumer remains the dominant retail theme.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings Aug 26 is the week's pivotal catalyst; street expects $95B revenue, $108B October guide
bullets.body: Jefferies expects NVDA to beat and raise when it reports August 26: July quarter revenue estimated at $95B vs. Street $91.9B, with October guidance of ~$108B (+14% QoQ) vs. Street $103.7B. Rubin ramp is the centerpiece, with ~13K+ racks in CY26 and 120K+ in CY27; Rubin overtakes Blackwell in 1QF28. HSBC raised its NVDA price target to $360 from $325. NVDA separately denied The Information report of China-specific LPU chip shipments, and separately agreed to license Poolside AI models for $6B plus a $1B investment.

bullets.title: MRVL elevated to key focus into Aug 27 earnings; Google deal implies $120B cumulative revenue through 2033
bullets.body: Multiple houses raised MRVL price targets ahead of its Aug 27 earnings report: Roth to $350, OpCo to $300, Oppenheimer to $300. MRVL revealed a commercial agreement with Google covering custom XPU attach products; Google warrants cover up to 59M shares implying $120B qualifying revenue through 2033. Custom AI ASIC sales are expected to double next year to $4B+ and exceed $10B by CY28. Jefferies models July quarter revenue at $2.8B vs. Street $2.7B with October guidance of $3.1B.

bullets.title: Private credit fragility watch: $1.4T market stabilized but macro downshift would reactivate stress
bullets.body: A Hedgeye framework call flagged the $1.4T private credit market as dormant but fragile. The 2025 First Brands and Tricolor failures, the early-2026 SaaS equity selloff hitting BDCs, and redemption surges at non-traded BDCs that breached repurchase caps revealed liquidity mismatches in semi-liquid vehicles. Conditions have since stabilized; a macro downshift is the key risk that would drive capital out of exposed financial equities.

bullets.title: ECB data-dependent; inflation expectations tick lower, wage growth slowing—September hike not certain
bullets.body: ECB's July Consumer Expectations Survey showed 1-year inflation expectations edging down to 2.9% (from 3.0%) and 3-year falling to 2.7%. ECB board member Kazaks said wage growth is gradually slowing and the bank is 'well placed to act if needed,' but stressed a September decision will be purely data-dependent. The UK composite PMI edged up to 52.5 in August with sticky services output prices, complicating MPC calculus.

bullets.title: Samsung unveils W100tr (~$72B) shareholder return plan; SK Hynix memory upcycle intact on HBM shortage
bullets.body: Samsung Electronics announced a ~W100-110 trillion (~$72-79B) shareholder return package for 2026E based on 50% of cumulative FCF, including ~W30tr in quarterly dividends and ~W15tr in buybacks. Citi projects a 6.4% dividend yield on common shares and 8.7% on preferred. SK Hynix separately reiterated its view that the memory upcycle is intact, driven by HBM shortages and KV cache demand; DRAM export unit prices for Aug 1-20 continued to rise. South Korea's Aug 1-20 semiconductor exports surged ~200% YoY.

bullets.title: US pressuring Netherlands to ban ASML China sales; Europe cedes frontier AI to US/China
bullets.body: The US is reportedly preparing to force the Netherlands to ban ASML from selling to China, adding to existing export controls. Separately, Europe has de facto conceded it cannot compete in frontier AI development: Mistral is pivoting to hosting Chinese open-weight models (including Z.ai's GLM-5.2) as a 'sovereign distribution guarantor,' redefining AI sovereignty as data-location control rather than model ownership. This creates geopolitical risk ahead of the October EU-China trade deadline.

bullets.title: Key events next week: Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29), NVDA/CRM/MRVL/INTU earnings, US PCE, China LPR
bullets.body: The macro and earnings calendar is dense: Fed Chairman Warsh speaks at Jackson Hole on Aug 28 at 10AM ET; NVDA reports Aug 26 after close ($2.09 EPS / $92B revenue consensus), CRM and WSM also report Aug 26, MRVL Aug 27, INTU Aug 25. US PCE and Eurozone CPI are due. JPMorgan notes post-midterm election seasonality historically shows +5.4% to +14.7% SPX returns at 3-12 month tenors with 78-100% hit rates.
